claims.quote: With nine compartments flooded the ship would still float, and as no known accident of the sea could possibly fill this many, the steamship *Titan* was considered practically unsinkable.
claims.description: A giant liner is claimed to be practically unsinkable thanks to watertight compartments, with no accident able to flood enough of them.

claims.quote: From the bridge, engine-room, and a dozen places on her deck the ninety-two doors of nineteen water-tight compartments could be closed in half a minute by turning a lever. These doors would also close automatically in the presence of water.
claims.description: Watertight compartment doors that close by lever from many stations and automatically when water is detected.

claims.quote: She was eight hundred feet long, of seventy thousand tons' displacement, seventy-five thousand horse-power, and on her trial trip had steamed at a rate of twenty-five knots an hour over the bottom
claims.description: An enormous 800-foot, 70,000-ton, 75,000-horsepower passenger liner sustaining 25 knots, far larger than ships then existing.

claims.quote: From her lofty bridge ran hidden telegraph lines to the bow, stern engine-room, crow's-nest on the foremast, and to all parts of the ship where work was done, each wire terminating in a marked dial with a movable indicator
claims.description: A shipboard telegraph/dial command system linking the bridge to all working stations, replacing shouted orders.

claims.quote: Unsinkable—indestructible, she carried as few boats as would satisfy the laws. These, twenty-four in number, were securely covered and lashed down to their chocks on the upper deck, and if launched would hold five hundred people.
claims.description: Because the ship is believed unsinkable, it carries lifeboats for only a fraction of the 3,000 aboard, a consequence of overconfidence in technology.

claims.quote: She would steam at full speed in fog, storm, and sunshine, and on the Northern Lane Route, winter and summer, for the following good and substantial reasons
claims.description: A shipping company adopts a policy of running at full speed regardless of fog or ice, a practice not yet openly followed.

claims.quote: in case of an end-on collision with an iceberg—the only thing afloat that she could not conquer—her bows would be crushed in but a few feet further at full than at half speed, and at the most three compartments would be flooded
claims.description: A claim that an iceberg collision at full speed would flood at most three compartments and not endanger the ship.

claims.quote: it was unofficially rumored among the two thousand passengers who had embarked at New York that an effort would now be made to do so.
claims.description: The liner is expected to cross the Atlantic from Sandy Hook to Ireland in under five days.

claims.quote: Cold is negative heat, and can be treated like radiant energy, decreasing as the square of the distance.
claims.description: Proposal that icebergs in fog could be located by calculating the rate of temperature decrease on approach.

claims.quote: that I may help to arouse such a sentiment of anger in the two countries as will forever end this wanton destruction of life and property for the sake of speed
claims.description: A hope that public outrage over a collision would end speed-driven ocean-liner recklessness for good.
